subject: history
title: Origins of the Second World War
welcome_lead: From Versailles to Munich, from appeasement to Poland in September 1939.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on the origins of WWII, appeasement and the Nazi-Soviet Pact.
final_note: You have crossed the bridge from Versailles to war.

concepts.def: British policy under Chamberlain of accommodating German revisionist demands to preserve peace.
Hitler's 7 March 1936 reoccupation of the demilitarised Rhineland in breach of Versailles and Locarno.
Union of Germany and Austria on 12 March 1938 following Nazi pressure on Schuschnigg.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hitler's aims combined revision of Versailles, racial Lebensraum in the East, and pursuit of European hegemony. Historians divide between intentionalists (Hugh Trevor-Roper) emphasising consistent plans expressed in Mein Kampf, and structuralists (Mason) stressing improvisation under domestic pressures. Hitler exploited British and French weariness, depression-era distractions and Soviet isolation.

Hitler abandoned the League in October 1933, reintroduced conscription in March 1935, signed the Anglo-German Naval Agreement in June 1935, remilitarised the Rhineland in March 1936, intervened in Spain from July 1936, annexed Austria in March 1938 and demanded the Sudetenland. At Munich on 29 September 1938 Chamberlain conceded; in March 1939 Hitler seized the rest of Czechoslovakia.

A.J.P. Taylor's Origins of the Second World War (1961) controversially portrayed Hitler as an opportunist. Defenders argue Britain rearmed (especially aircraft) and lacked allies; critics including Churchill saw appeasement as moral failure that emboldened Hitler. The Nazi-Soviet Pact of 23 August 1939 made war inevitable; Britain honoured its Polish guarantee on 3 September.

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.
Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
The League failed because no countries joined it.

mcqs.q: Did the Treaty of Versailles directly cause WWII?
options: Versailles caused WWII directly because it was so harsh on Germany.
Versailles caused WWII because it required Germany to invade Poland.
It contributed via German resentment and economic strain, but the 1930s Depression, Hitler's choices, and Allied appeasement were equally necessary — Versailles alone is not sufficient.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
